ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Jim Bridger Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: Establishing primary care for two years of blurred vision in both eyes with glare: vision, falls, driving, chronic low back pain at an old arrow-wound site, a goiter, sore knees, mood, and an ophthalmology consultation. Concerns: He can no longer see faces, the ground at dusk or the road at night, and is afraid of losing his sight altogether; An old ache in his lower back where the arrow went in, and sore knees on the orchard slopes; He wants to keep working his orchard, riding and driving into town. [S]

Plain X-ray of the lumbar spine, anteroposterior and lateral: multilevel disc-space narrowing and osteophytes from L3 to S1, worst at L4-L5; facet arthropathy at L4-L5 and L5-S1; normal alignment; no fracture; no metallic or other radiopaque foreign body in the soft tissues

Dilated fundus examination with indirect ophthalmoscopy, both eyes: healthy optic discs (cup-to-disc 0.3 in each eye), flat maculas without drusen or hemorrhage, no diabetic retinopathy, attached retinas; the view of the right fundus hazy through the dense lens
Optical coherence tomography of the macula, both eyes: normal foveal contour and thickness; no fluid, drusen or epiretinal membrane
Optical biometry (partial coherence interferometry) of both eyes for lens implant power, with keratometry; regular corneas without significant astigmatism

Ultrasound of the thyroid: enlarged gland with several nodules in both lobes; the largest, 1.6 cm in the left lobe, is spongiform (very low suspicion); the others are under 1 cm, isoechoic or mixed cystic, with no microcalcifications; no enlarged neck nodes; trachea midline

Phacoemulsification of the right cataract with a posterior chamber intraocular lens in the capsular bag, under topical and intracameral anesthesia with light sedation, as day surgery; intracameral antibiotic; no complications

Phacoemulsification of the left cataract with a posterior chamber intraocular lens in the capsular bag, under topical and intracameral anesthesia with light sedation, as day surgery; intracameral antibiotic; no complications
Plain X-ray of the right wrist with scaphoid views: no fracture or dislocation; soft-tissue swelling over the back of the wrist; mild degenerative change at the base of the thumb
Advance care planning conversation, about 20 minutes, with his consent

tr.td: Arrow wounds to the back in a fight; the iron head of one arrow stayed in his back for about three years
A three-inch iron arrowhead, hooked on a bone and walled in by tissue, cut out of his back by a missionary physician at a fur traders' rendezvous
Rheumatism hampering his movements during his last years of scouting
Failing eyesight since his early sixties, worse over the past year; cause not recorded

list.item: Gradual, painless blurring of vision in both eyes over about two years, worse in the right, with glare from sunlight and oncoming headlights, faded colors, and trouble recognizing faces across a room; Snellen acuity 20/200 right and 20/100 left with his old glasses, no better with a pinhole; no flashes, floaters, pain or redness; cause under evaluation with an ophthalmology consultation: resolved, confirmed [S]

Bilateral age-related nuclear cataract, dense and brunescent in the right eye and moderate in the left, with cortical spokes; the cause of his reduced vision, glare and color loss; no glaucoma, macular degeneration or diabetic retinopathy; treated with sequential cataract surgery: resolved, confirmed [S]

Chronic low back pain for many years, aching across the lower back and worst on the side of an old arrow-wound scar over the right lower back, stiff in the morning and after long rides in his truck; no leg pain, numbness, weakness, bladder or bowel change, fever or weight loss; no red flags: active, confirmed [S]

Nontoxic multinodular goiter, present for decades: a firm, nodular, non-tender thyroid enlargement with no pressure symptoms (no trouble swallowing or breathing, no voice change); euthyroid: active, confirmed [S]
Primary osteoarthritis of both knees, aching on stairs and after walking the orchard, with morning stiffness under half an hour, crepitus and bony enlargement: active, confirmed [S]
One fall in the past year, missing the bottom step of the porch at dusk, without injury; poor vision in low light and contrast; at risk of further falls: active, confirmed [S]
Sprain of the right wrist from a fall on the porch steps three weeks after the first cataract operation, when the two eyes saw differently; X-ray without fracture; healed: resolved, confirmed [S]

Lens implants in both eyes after sequential phacoemulsification cataract surgery, right then left six weeks apart; best-corrected vision about 20/20 in each eye with new glasses: active, confirmed [S]

tr.td: Establishing primary care for two years of blurred vision in both eyes with glare: vision, falls, driving, chronic low back pain at an old arrow-wound site, a goiter, sore knees, mood, and an ophthalmology consultation
Two-week review on the day of the ophthalmology consultation: the eye examination and the surgical plan, the lumbar X-ray, the thyroid ultrasound and back exercise
Six-week review four weeks after right cataract surgery: vision, the drops, falls between operations, back pain and the wrist
Fifteen-week review five weeks after left cataract surgery: vision with new glasses, driving, back pain and knees
Six-month review: back pain on a home program, knees, falls, the goiter and the plan ahead
Same-day sick visit for a right wrist injury after a fall

Vision work-up at intake: visual acuity with and without pinhole, pupils, red reflex and a functional history (faces, reading signs, driving, glare, falls); HbA1c for diabetic retinopathy risk; urgent eye care for any sudden loss, pain or redness
Ophthalmology consultation (cataract) for a comprehensive dilated eye examination, intraocular pressure and macular OCT, the cause of the vision loss, and surgical candidacy

Cataract surgery: phacoemulsification with a monofocal lens implant aimed at distance in the right eye, the worse eye, then the left eye about six weeks later; optical biometry and keratometry beforehand; immediately sequential bilateral surgery discussed and not chosen; postoperative antibiotic and steroid drops with checks at one day, one to two weeks and one month; extra care on steps while the two eyes see differently between operations; new glasses after the second eye
Falls and low vision: brighter lighting on the porch and stairs, contrast tape on step edges, a second handrail, night lights; no driving until vision meets the state standard

Low back pain: lumbar X-ray at intake to look for a retained fragment at the old wound (and to clear any later MRI); reassurance and staying active; physical therapy with exercise and motor control training, then a home program, with heat; no opioids, no muscle relaxants; a short course of an oral anti-inflammatory only if exercise is not enough

Goiter: TSH and free T4; thyroid ultrasound with the sonographic pattern of each nodule; fine-needle aspiration only for a nodule that meets size and pattern thresholds; follow-up ultrasound at an interval set by the findings; return for trouble swallowing or breathing, voice change or rapid growth
Knees: quadriceps strengthening, walking and tai chi; topical diclofenac; a stick in the outside hand on slopes
Instructions by ear: every plan explained aloud with teach-back, medicine schedules recorded as voice reminders and shown by demonstration, and large-print copies for his household
Find the cause of the blurred vision
Bilateral age-related cataract; glaucoma, macular degeneration and diabetic retinopathy excluded
See well enough to recognize faces, walk safely at dusk and meet the vision standard for driving
Best-corrected vision about 20/20 in each eye after sequential surgery; cleared to drive by day and night
One fall with a wrist sprain between the two operations; none since, with handrails, step edging and better light
Back pain at 3 or less out of 10 and back to a full day in the orchard
Average pain 6 to 2 out of 10 on exercise therapy without opioids
Keep the goiter under watch without unnecessary tests
Euthyroid; no nodule meets the threshold for biopsy; repeat ultrasound in about two years
